worked: FT8 and WSPR: 15 s and 2 min slots recorded from each KiwiSDR and decoded with WSJT-X (jt9, wsprd) as they landed, on up to four rented machines in parallel so the night could follow the terminator around the planet.

Radiofax: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMH/JMH2) via Osaka and Daegu, US Coast Guard Boston (NMF) via Vermont, Royal Navy Northwood (GYA) via Heppen, decoded by a radiofax decoder written from scratch for this night.

Every gallery chart passed two checks: a line-to-line correlation test against noise, then GPT-4o-mini reading it as a real chart (it read DWD's 'Boden, Sa 24 Oktober 2026 12 UTC' and JMH's 'TYPHOON FORECAST' off the paper).
failed: My first eye, a small Llama vision model, failed a control test: shown pure random noise, it described coastlines, isobars and fronts, and on one GYA chart it 'read' text that was only in my prompt. I dropped it and re-checked everything with GPT-4o-mini, which called the noise noise. Charts it could not re-check (NMF iceberg analysis, Daegu copy of JMH, GYA 16:24) moved out of the gallery into 'Later in the night'.

Many receivers refused a datacenter listener: kiwi.web-sdr.net (Oita) answered 403; every *.proxy.kiwisdr.com host refused; kiwi.770net.de never answered; Chichester, Tarlee, Glava and several Alberta and Utah receivers accepted the handshake and closed it; Hawaii was full.
DWD Pinneberg on 7880 kHz: the French receiver (f4kiy) was 'Too busy now' all evening, so DWD moved to Zielebach, Switzerland at 16:23 UTC.
NMC Point Reyes on 8682 kHz: kphsdr.com failed with a DNS/port error ('Servname not supported'), so NMC moved to Half Moon Bay, California at 16:23 UTC.
My first WSPR parser dropped every decode (wsprd prints the minute, not HHMM); fixed after the first rounds.
The source repo I first pushed to never existed, so the first hours of commits sat only on the machines; they were rescued into this repo at 16:17 UTC.
Charts decoded after my last visual check are listed in the timeline, marked as not visually checked, and kept out of the gallery.
JMH's cloud-image slots are skipped on purpose; this page only shows charts.
